c.tagline: Garden City reborn — a low-slung, creative gateway to the Southern Alps.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares vary by company (Blue Star and Gold Band are the main operators); agree a fixed price for airport transfers or use the Purple Line bus or rideshare instead.

emergency.note: 111 is the single nationwide emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; Christchurch Hospital runs the city's main public emergency department.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Late at night the bar strips around the central city (Manchester/Colombo Street area) can get rowdy; usual weekend-night awareness.

hood_desc: The rebuilt heart around Cathedral Square, the Terraces on the Avon, Riverside Market and the heritage tram loop; best for first-timers who want the museums, restaurants and shopping all within walking distance.

A leafy inner suburb along Riccarton Road with Westfield Riccarton mall, the historic Riccarton House & Bush and the busy Sunday Riccarton Market; good-value stays and plenty of eateries near the university.
An upscale, tree-lined northern suburb with boutique shopping, cafes and restaurants along Papanui Road; suits travelers wanting a refined, quiet base a short hop from the centre.
A revived inner-west district around the Addington Raceway and Wigram, full of craft breweries, restaurants and live-music venues; handy to the stadium and events traffic.
A relaxed seaside village about 12 km east with a sandy surf beach, the landmark Cave Rock and a strip of beachfront cafes; suits those wanting coast and calm over city bustle.
lodging: Chateau on the Park - DoubleTree by Hilton Christchurch

water.note: Tap water is safe and high quality throughout the city.

sys.n: Metro Bus network (including the Orbiter and Purple Line)

transit.pay: Tap on and off with a Metrocard (a reloadable smartcard sold at the central Bus Interchange and selected retailers) or pay the cash fare to the driver; the Metrocard adult fare is about NZ$2 versus roughly NZ$4 cash, with free transfers within two hours. The heritage tram is a separate tourist service with its own ticket.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am to about 11pm on core routes, with reduced weekend and evening frequency; there is no commuter rail and no true 24-hour network, so taxis or rideshare cover the late hours.
transit.note: Christchurch has no metro or commuter rail — the flat, spread-out city is served entirely by Metro buses fanning out from the central Bus Interchange, supplemented by the tourist-oriented heritage tram loop through the city centre.

train: TranzAlpine scenic train to Greymouth via Arthur's Pass
Coastal Pacific scenic train to Picton via Kaikōura

transit.m: Metro Purple Line bus to the central Bus Interchange (~50 min, every 30 min)

tip.r: Not expected; tipping is uncommon in New Zealand, though rounding up or leaving a little for exceptional service is appreciated.
